title: RETURN 1 / RETURN 2 — alternate return jumps to a caller-supplied label
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE PARSE(LINE, *, *)
C     Two of the formal arguments are '*' (alternate return
C     placeholders). The body's RETURN 1 jumps to the first '*'
C     argument the caller supplied (a label like *100). RETURN 2
C     jumps to the second. F90 marked alternate return obsolescent;
C     F2008 deleted it.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      CHARACTER*80 LINE
      IF (LINE(1:1) .EQ. '#') THEN
         RETURN 1
C                ^ caller's first alternate label
      END IF
      IF (LEN_TRIM(LINE) .EQ. 0) THEN
         RETURN 2
C                ^ caller's second alternate label
      END IF
      RETURN
      END
notes: Alternate return is a hidden control-flow construct: callers branch based on which '*' argument the callee picks. A Java/C# rewrite usually returns an enum (PARSED, COMMENT, BLANK). The spec must enumerate ALL alternate-return paths so the rewrite enum covers each.
